correctness.rationale: The frozen proof correctly identifies closed-neighborhood complements inside each part, so same-part pair weights are binomial coefficients on \(n_i-2\) vertices while cross-part weights vanish for \(k\ge1\). A maximum-weight spanning tree can simultaneously use \(n_i-1\) positive-weight edges inside every non-singleton part and connect the resulting components with zero-weight cross-part edges. Non-dominating \(k\)-sets are exactly proper \(k\)-subsets contained in one part, and the per-part binomial simplification gives the stated nonnegative residual and the sharp equality criterion. An independent bounded replay checked the residual identity for every multipartite integer partition through order 12; the package verifier independently enumerates domination sets and maximum spanning trees through order 11.
risks: The theorem excludes \(k=0\), where cross-part avoidance intersections no longer have zero weight; no claim is made there.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact sharpness analysis of a newly introduced correction on a canonical dense graph family. It identifies exactly when the pairwise correction is already complete and quantifies the entire remaining higher-order deficit when it is not, directly addressing the source paper's family-specific correction question rather than merely recomputing a known domination count.
risks: Its scope is one graph family and one overlap correction; it does not provide a universal higher-order scheme.

limitations: Finite simple complete multipartite graphs only, with at least two nonempty parts and \(1\le k\le N\); the residual is a total deficit, not a canonical decomposition into all higher-order intersections.
